ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure there is a large square, with an uncolored small square at each of the four corners; in the middle of each side there is also an uncolored triangle, and the vertices of these four triangles are all at the center of the large square. The gray shaded parts are the four regions sandwiched between these small squares at the corners and the middle triangles. Reasoning: The area of the large square is 16 cm², so the side length is 4 cm. The area of each small square at the corners is 1 cm², so the side length is 1 cm. Therefore the base length of the uncolored triangle in the middle of each side is 4 - 1 - 1 = 2 cm. The height of this triangle from the side to the center of the square is 2 cm, so the area of each middle triangle is (1/2) × 2 × 2 = 2 cm². The total area of four such triangles is 8 cm². The total area of the small squares at the four corners is 4 × 1 = 4 cm². Therefore the uncolored area is altogether 8 + 4 = 12 cm², and the shaded area is 16 - 12 = 4 cm².

method.method_draft: Use a complement decomposition. First read from the image that the large square has four unshaded 1-by-1 corner squares and four unshaded triangular regions in the middle of the sides, all meeting at the central point; the shaded regions are the four remaining congruent corner-adjacent pieces. From the text, the large square area is 16 cm^2, so its side length is 4 cm, and each small corner square has side length 1 cm. Therefore each middle-side unshaded triangle has base 4 - 1 - 1 = 2 cm along a side of the large square and height 2 cm from that side to the center of the large square. Its area is (1/2)(2)(2)=2 cm^2, so the four such triangles total 8 cm^2. The four corner squares total 4 cm^2. Subtract unshaded area from the large square: 16 - 8 - 4 = 4 cm^2.

method.method_draft: Compute one shaded piece directly and multiply by symmetry. From the image, the four shaded pieces are congruent by rotational symmetry. Set coordinates on the large square with corners (0,0), (4,0), (4,4), and (0,4). The top-left small square has side 1, so its relevant vertices are (0,3), (1,3), and (1,4), and the central intersection is at (2,2). The top-left shaded piece is the polygon bounded by (0,3), (1,3), (1,4), and (2,2). Its area can be found by the shoelace formula, or equivalently as triangle with vertices (0,3), (1,4), (2,2) minus the right triangle half of the 1-by-1 corner square. The larger triangle has area 3/2 cm^2 and the half-corner triangle has area 1/2 cm^2, leaving 1 cm^2 for one shaded piece. Multiply by 4 shaded pieces to get 4 cm^2.
